pairs.why: A's feeder fills more of the card with the rope hanger running up to the top edge, like the real feeder that dominates the frame. B's feeder is smaller and floats with more empty background.
A's locker is large and set slightly left of centre with its door opening to the right, as in the real card, and it fills the frame about as much as B does.
A's calculator has the real card's stocky tilted footprint, a perspective top-left to bottom-right, and a similar fill. B is a narrower, taller slab.
A's ship sits on the card with a similar fill and side margins to the real one. B's hull runs closer to the edges and its flags crowd the top.
A's cap spans about the same width as the real cap and keeps floor around it. B's cap is oversized and nearly touches the right edge.
A's anchor is tilted and fills the frame with margins close to the real card's. B's oversized ring and balls crowd the top.
B's table is bigger and off-centre with the stools unevenly placed, which is nearer the real card's close, cropped framing. A is a small, symmetric, pulled-back set.
A's calculator has the real card's wide tilted footprint and fill. B is a tall, narrow slab with a different tilt.
